crossRefs.note: To Adam he said, “Because you have listened to your wife’s voice, and ate from the tree, about which I commanded you…
The appetite of the laboring man labors for him; for his mouth urges him on.
Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body…
Don’t work for the food which perishes, but for the food which remains to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give…
But godliness with contentment is great gain.
If a man fathers a hundred children, and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his soul is not…
He who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he who loves abundance, with increase: this also is vanity.
I will tell my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Take your ease, eat, drink, and be merry.” ’

translations.web: All the labor of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
translations.bsb: All a man’s labor is for his mouth, yet his appetite is never satisfied.
